44616.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
44616.question_text: The action that portrayed Moses as a leader of the Israelites was his
44616.explanation:
Moses' action of killing an Egyptian who was beating a Hebrew is a key event that portrays Moses as a leader. This act marked a decisive moment in his life, where he took action to defend his people (the Israelites). Although this act was impulsive and resulted in Moses fleeing to Midian, it is an important indication of his growing awareness of his role in delivering the Israelites.

Exodus 2:11-12 (RSV):

“One day, when Moses had grown up, he went out to his people and looked on their burdens; and he saw an Egyptian beating a Hebrew, one of his own people. He looked this way and that, and seeing no one, he slew the Egyptian and hid him in the sand.”

This act of defending his people set the stage for Moses' eventual leadership role in delivering the Israelites from slavery in Egypt.

Killing of an Egyptian who fought with a Hebrew.

44625.question_text: Believers today are partakers of the New Covenant through
44625.explanation:
Believers today are partakers of the New Covenant through the gift of the Spirit. This is based on what is described in Acts 2:38 and Ezekiel 36:26-27, where the Holy Spirit is given to believers as part of the fulfillment of the New Covenant. In the New Covenant, God's laws are written on the hearts of His people, and the Holy Spirit empowers believers to live in accordance with God's will.

The New Covenant is marked by the inner transformation that comes through the Holy Spirit, and this is available to all who accept Christ as their Savior.

44635.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
44635.question_text: What effect did the decision of the Council of Jerusalem have on the Early Church?
44635.explanation:
The Council of Jerusalem (Acts 15) was an important moment in the early Christian church. The council addressed a major issue: whether Gentile (non-Jewish) converts to Christianity needed to adhere to Jewish laws, particularly circumcision, to be fully accepted into the Christian community.

The decision of the council was that Gentiles did not have to follow the Jewish laws (like circumcision) to be Christians, allowing them to become full members of the church without adopting all Jewish customs. This freed Gentiles to join the Christian community, making the church more inclusive and paving the way for the spread of Christianity beyond Jewish circles.

options.text: The Jews became leaders of the community
The church experienced freedom from persecution
Gentiles were free to be members

''.....I am the LORD, and there is no other, beside me there is no God....''

God's statement above through Isaiah depicts
44639.explanation:
The statement "I am the LORD, and there is no other, beside me there is no God..." is from Isaiah 45:5, and it emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of God. This is a declaration of His supreme power and authority, asserting that there is no other deity beside Him. He is the only true God, and His reign is unchallenged.

This reflects God's sovereignty over all creation, as He is the ultimate ruler and supreme authority, not just over Israel, but over everything in existence.
